<x_0.04><y_0.0742>## _456. Conferve of the leaves of garden feurvy-grafs._ L.<x_0.8076><y_0.0938><class_Section-header>

<x_0.0234><y_0.0922>This is the only form that feurvy-grafs in fubilance can be kept in without the total lois of its virtues. The conferve retains the full tafte and virtue of the herb for a very confiderable length of time, as a year or two, provided the veffel be made perfectly clofe and fet in a cool place. It may be given in feorbutic habits three or four times a-day, or oftener.<x_0.8242><y_0.1922><class_Text>

<x_0.0732><y_0.1969>## _457. Conferve of the leaves of wood-forrel._ L.<x_0.7734><y_0.2156><class_Section-header>

<x_0.0215><y_0.2148>This is a very elegant and grateful conferve; in tafte it is lightly acidulous, with a peculiar flavour, which fome refemble to that of green-tea. It is taken occasionally for quenching thirft, and cooling the mouth and fauces, in hot dittempers. It may be ufefully joined to the foregoing preparation, whole virtue it fomewhat promotes, at the fame time that it improves the tafte.<x_0.8223><y_0.3289><class_Text>

<x_0.083><y_0.3312>### _458. Conferve of the leaves of fpearmint._ L.<x_0.7617><y_0.3516><class_Section-header>

<x_0.0195><y_0.3508>The conferve of mint retains the tafte and virtues of the herb. It is given in weakness of the flomach and retchings to vomit ; and not unfrequently does service in fome cafes of this kind, where the warmer and more active preparations of mint would be less proper.<x_0.8213><y_0.4383><class_Text>

<x_0.125><y_0.4391>## _459. Conferve of the leaves of rue._ L.<x_0.7158><y_0.457><class_Section-header>

<x_0.0186><y_0.4562>This conferve is given from a dram to half an ounce in crudities of the prime vice, for promoting digestion, and in hyfteric diforders: it gently fituates the folids, attenuates vifcid juices, and excites the natural fecretions. Some have had a great opinion of it, taken in a morning, as a prefervative against the effects of contagious air or exbalation.<x_0.8203><y_0.5578><class_Text>

<x_0.0615><y_0.5602>## _460. Conferve of the tops of fea-wormwood._ L.<x_0.7686><y_0.5789><class_Section-header>

<x_0.0127><y_0.5781>The conferve of wormwood has been celebrated in dropflies: Matthiolus relates, that feveral perfons were cured by it of that ditemper, without the afflitance of any other medicine. Where the diforder indeed proceeds from a limple laxity or flaceidity of the folids, the continued ufe of this medicine may be of fome service, as it appears to be a not inclegant mild corroborant. It is directed to be given in the dofe of half an ounce, about three hours before meals.<x_0.8184><y_0.7055><class_Text>

<x_0.0889><y_0.7094>## _461. Conferve of the buds of red roofs._ L.<x_0.7275><y_0.7266><class_Section-header>

<x_0.0107><y_0.7242>This is a very agreeable and useful conferve. A dram or two, diffolved in warm milk, are frequently given as a light reftringent in weaknefs of the flo- mach, and likewise in coughs and phthifical complaints. In the German Ephemerides, examples are related of very dangerous phthifes cured by the con- tinued ufe of this medicine : in one of thefe cafes, 20 pounds of the conferve were taken in the space of a month; and in another, upwards of 30. Riverius mentions several other influences of this kind.<x_0.8174><y_0.8664><class_Text>
